newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa says no talks under way with UAP.
newsitem.headline: Axa says no talks under way with UAP.

text.p: French insurer Axa said on Wednesday that no discussions were under way with rival UAP, whose shares have been boosted recently by speculation that Axa was eyeing it as a takeover target.
"We are not in any discussions with UAP," Axa chairman Claude Bebear said at a news conference where he announced that first-half results climbed 51.8 percent to 1.98 billion francs.
Bebear, who recently declared that the group had a 30 billion franc war chest, also said there were no talks of any importance under way with other groups.
"At the moment we are in no discussions of any significance with anyone," he said.
He said he was regularly approached by merchant banks with proposals.
"They talk to us not only about UAP but also about a lot of other companies," Bebear said. "They're just doing their job."
Analysts have said low profitability at Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) makes it an unlikely takeover target for Axa.
They have also estimated that a takeover of UAP would cost about 30 billion francs which they said would be too big for Axa to swallow even if it has a war chest of the same amount.
